Human Learning & Development: The person reads the comments and sorts them: valid complaints about bugs, misunderstandings that can be clarified, and pure abuse that deserves no reply and possibly a report to the platform.
The founder argues point by point with critics and attacks their motives. Screenshots circulate, and the argument draws far more attention than the original complaint.
The team replies politely, thanks the user for raising the issue, explains what will be fixed and by when, then follows up publicly after the fix, which turns some critics into supporters.

Subtype: Approach: taking the conversation to private channels [Action]
Human Learning & Development: For a customer-specific complaint, the company offers a direct call or email for details and returns later to say the matter was resolved, protecting privacy and avoiding a public fight.

Subtype: Approach: ignoring everything and hoping it fades [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: The company stays silent about a real safety complaint. Silence reads as indifference, more users join in and a local issue becomes a wider reputation problem.

Subtype: Approach: seeking a trusted friend's view [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Before posting a response, the person shares the draft with a friend not emotionally involved, who suggests removing sarcasm and adding a concrete promise.

Subtype: Approach: protecting mental health while the storm passes [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: The person mutes notifications for two days, avoids checking metrics every hour, and talks with family, recognising that attention will move on and worth is not defined by strangers.

Subtype: Approach: using legal remedies only for real harm [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: When some posts contain false and harmful claims, the person collects screenshots and consults a lawyer about lawful options, but does not threaten critics over honest disagreement.

Subtype: Approach: updating the product and process after the episode [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The team adds a support form, a public changelog and a quicker reply time, reasoning that most future public complaints can be handled earlier if channels for feedback exist.

Subtype: Approach: clarifying what the mentee needs [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Before agreeing to mentor a college student, the young engineer asks about goals and challenges, realising that the student needs interview practice more than technical lectures.

Subtype: Approach: setting a simple recurring schedule [Action]
Human Learning & Development: The mentor and mentee meet for forty minutes every second Sunday with an agenda shared beforehand, and each session ends with one small task for the next time.

Subtype: Approach: giving answers instead of guiding [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: The mentor solves each problem for the mentee to be helpful. The mentee gets fast results but does not learn to think, and returns with the same kind of problem again.

Subtype: Approach: asking questions to build thinking [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Instead of giving the solution, the mentor asks what has been tried, what the options are and how each might fail, guiding the mentee to reason through the problem.
The mentor describes a past bad project and what was learned, which helps the mentee feel safe admitting mistakes, though the mentor also avoids making the story about themselves.
The mentor gives confident advice on higher studies abroad without knowing the process. The mentee follows it and misses deadlines, showing why it is fine for a mentor to admit not knowing.

Subtype: Approach: connecting the mentee to other people [Action]
Human Learning & Development: When a question falls outside the mentor's area, the mentor introduces the mentee to a friend who works in that field, widening the mentee's network and support.

Subtype: Approach: adapting to the mentee's style and background [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The mentor notices a first-generation graduate is shy about asking questions, so switches to written notes before meetings and allows quiet time, adapting to the person rather than the plan.

Subtype: Approach: guarding own time and limits [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Knowing that overcommitting leads to missed sessions, the mentor takes only two mentees at a time and states availability clearly, keeping the commitment reliable.

Subtype: Approach: reviewing progress and ending gracefully [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After six months, the mentor and mentee review goals achieved, decide what remains, and agree to shift to occasional check-ins, treating the end of regular sessions as success and not as abandonment.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Human Learning & Development: The person asks which problems keep drawing attention, such as rural education or clean water, and which of them fit their skills, before choosing a project to work on.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: starting with a small pilot [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A software worker begins by teaching free weekend coding classes to twenty students in a nearby village school, learning what works before planning anything larger.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: grand vision with no first step [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: The person dreams of transforming education across the state, spends months on presentations and logos, and never starts. The size of the dream makes any first action seem too small.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: listening to the community before designing [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Before starting a library, the person talks with parents and teachers in the village and learns that reliable evening lighting and study space matter more than new books.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: planning for sustainability and handover [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: The person asks who will run the project when they are busy or move away, and trains a local volunteer, arranging small recurring funding so that it does not depend on one person.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Human Learning & Development: The person builds computer labs in a school without power backup or trained teachers. The equipment sits unused, showing how good intentions without local fit produce little benefit.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Human Learning & Development: The organiser records attendance, test scores and student feedback each month, using them to decide whether to continue, adjust or stop each activity.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: transparent accounts and legal setup [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Handling donations, the organiser registers a trust with legal help, keeps clear records and shares accounts with donors, protecting trust and following the law.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Subtype: Approach: balancing the project with job and health [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Noticing burnout after three months of late nights, the person limits the project to fixed weekly hours and invites more volunteers, understanding that a purpose lasts only if its carrier does.

Subtopic: Planning a legacy or purpose project
Human Learning & Development: After a year, data shows that the weekend classes reach few girls. The person adds a timing for mothers' approval and a women teacher, adapting the plan to evidence from the community.

Subtype: Approach: starts from the finished picture and asks what comes just before it [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A child who wants a built block tower looks at the picture on the box and asks what goes on top, then what goes under that, and so picks the base blocks first.

Subtype: Approach: counts back from a fixed date to set small deadlines [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A girl with a Friday science fair counts back: poster done Thursday, experiment run Tuesday, materials bought Sunday. She writes each date on a sticky note on her desk.

Subtype: Approach: fixes the target score and derives weekly study targets from it [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A Class 11 student aiming for 90 percent in physics estimates marks needed per unit, sees which chapters lag, and sets weekly chapter and problem counts from the exam date.

Subtype: Approach: assumes only the last step is known and chains backwards [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A final-year student wants a product-company job and works back neatly, but never checks whether the earlier steps are actually achievable. The chain looks tidy while the first step stays vague.

Subtype: Approach: rechecks the backward chain against real progress and reschedules [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A young analyst planning a CFA path sees the month-three checkpoint slipping. She re-derives later milestones from the exam date and drops one optional certification.

Subtype: Approach: combines backward planning with buffers and a checklist [Action]
Human Learning & Development: An engineer launching a small app works back from a festival-season release date, adds two weeks of slack before it, and tracks each dependent task on a shared checklist.

Subtype: Approach: imagines the plan has already failed and lists reasons [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Before a school fest stall, a teenager asks what if it flopped, and writes: no change ready, rain, poor location. Naming causes in advance surfaces risks that hopeful planning skipped.

Subtype: Approach: turns each imagined failure into a preventive step [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student team planning a hackathon entry imagines losing, lists weak internet and one person doing all the code, then books a hotspot and splits modules among three people.

Subtype: Approach: imagines so many failures that starting feels impossible [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a startup lists fifty ways it could collapse and feels dread. Without ranking the risks by likelihood and damage, the exercise becomes a reason to avoid beginning.

Subtype: Approach: runs a short team pre-mortem before a client demo [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A team lead asks each colleague to write privately why tomorrow's demo would fail. Quiet members raise data-loading and login risks that the confident planners had not mentioned.

Subtype: Approach: ranks imagined failures and revises the plan around the top three [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After a pre-mortem, a manager notices the list is unfocused. She keeps the three risks that are both likely and costly, plans mitigations for those, and accepts the rest.

Subtype: Approach: picks a tool that closes the gap in front of them [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A child wants the biscuit tin on a high shelf and drags over a stool. The gap is height, and the stool is the means that reduces it, though the tin remains heavy.

Subtype: Approach: compares where things are with where they should be and picks a step that shrinks the gap [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy wants his cycle at school but the tyre is flat. Gap: no air. Step: find the pump. Then the next gap is the tyre valve, so he asks his father for the adapter.

Subtype: Approach: breaks a large gap into subgoals when the direct step is blocked [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student needs to reach a coaching centre across town but has no lift. Subgoal: get to the bus stop, then the bus number, then the fare. Each subgoal is solvable alone.

Subtype: Approach: keeps closing the nearest gap and never steps back to check the route [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student repeatedly fixes the loudest problem in a project, such as a bug, then a slide, then a formatting issue, and drifts away from the main requirement until the deadline.

Subtype: Approach: notices a dead end and sets a temporary detour subgoal [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: An engineer stuck because a needed library will not install pauses, sets a subgoal of testing in a container, and returns to the original gap once the environment works.

Subtype: Approach: tries the same action in different ways until something works [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A toddler tries to fit a round block into a square hole, turns it, presses harder, then moves to the round hole and it drops in. The success teaches without any words.

Subtype: Approach: tests several options and remembers which worked [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A child building a paper boat tries folding it three ways and floats each in a bucket. The one with a wider base stays upright, so she folds that one from then on.

Subtype: Approach: makes small changes one at a time and watches the result [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy tuning his kite changes the tail length, then the string position. Because he alters one thing per flight, he learns that the longer tail steadies it.

Subtype: Approach: random changes with no record of what was tried [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager fixing a phone's slow Wi-Fi flips settings at random, forgets which he changed, and ends up worse off. Without notes, error gives no reliable learning.

Subtype: Approach: switches to noting each attempt and its outcome [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A student debugging code after a night of random edits starts a log of what he changed and what happened, and finds the fault within twenty minutes.

Subtype: Approach: uses safe cheap trials when testing is inexpensive and mistakes are recoverable [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A new cook adjusts spices across several small pots of dal rather than one big batch. Cheap, reversible trials let her explore quickly without wasting much.

Subtype: Approach: picks the first option that is good enough and stops looking [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A girl needs a cover for her notebook and takes the first plain one that fits and is not torn, instead of checking every shelf at the stationery shop.

Subtype: Approach: sets a minimum standard in advance and chooses the first option that meets it [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager choosing a study spot decides it must be quiet, have a table and be within ten minutes. The second place he checks meets all three, so he takes it.

Subtype: Approach: uses good enough for low-stakes decisions to save mental energy [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A hostel student chooses a laptop bag by two criteria, price under a limit and a padded pocket, and stops. Saving hours of comparison leaves time for exam preparation.

Subtype: Approach: sets the bar too low on an important decision [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional accepts the first flat that meets basic needs but skips checking the lease terms and the commute. The threshold fit a cheap purchase and did not fit a year-long commitment.

Subtype: Approach: raises the threshold after noticing the stakes and rechecks options [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Realising a rental is a big commitment, she adds criteria such as noise, water supply and landlord reputation, and visits two more flats before deciding.

Subtype: Approach: scores options against weighted criteria in a table [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student picking a stream after Class 10 lists interest, job outlook, effort and distance of college. He weights them, scores each stream and compares the totals.

Subtype: Approach: builds the matrix in a spreadsheet and adjusts weights to see how the ranking changes [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student comparing three job offers puts salary, learning, location and growth in columns, then changes weights to test whether the winner holds up.

Subtype: Approach: fudges scores to make the matrix confirm a favourite [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student who already loves one college gives it high scores on subjective criteria and low scores on rivals. The tidy numbers look objective but hide a decision made beforehand.

Subtype: Approach: uses the matrix to expose which criterion truly drives a choice [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A young couple comparing flats notices that whichever weights they use, commute time decides the outcome, which shows them what they actually care about.

Subtype: Approach: notices a gut feeling against the top score and revisits the criteria [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: When a matrix favours a job she dreads, she asks what is missing, adds team culture and daily work as criteria, and the ranking changes.

Subtype: Approach: solves a new problem by comparing it with a familiar one [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A child who cannot open a new jar remembers that her mother twists the lid of the pickle jar, and she copies that turning motion.

Subtype: Approach: uses an earlier solved problem as a model for a new one [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy asked to share cricket turns among five friends recalls how the class used a roll-number order for the library, and sets up a rotating list.

Subtype: Approach: explains an unfamiliar idea through a familiar comparison [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student stuck on electric current thinks of water flowing through pipes, with voltage as pressure and resistance as a narrow pipe, and can then reason about circuits.

Subtype: Approach: borrows a superficially similar case that differs in the key feature [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a campus food stall copies a cafe's pricing and hours, but ignores that the cafe sits on a busy road while his stall serves a quiet hostel block.

Subtype: Approach: tests where the analogy breaks and adjusts the borrowed plan [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A manager applying last year's hiring plan checks what has changed, finds the market tighter, and shortens the timeline while keeping the interview structure.

Subtype: Approach: asks what basic facts must be true rather than following the usual way [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy told his plant needs fertiliser asks what plants really need. He learns water, light and soil, checks those three, and finds the pot has no drainage.

Subtype: Approach: strips a problem to its physical or logical basics before choosing a method [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teen designing a simple cooler for the summer asks how heat leaves a body, then uses damp cloth for evaporation rather than copying a store design.

Subtype: Approach: rebuilds a cost estimate from basic quantities instead of market price [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student pricing a mess service works out grain, gas, labour and waste per plate, and finds where the usual price is inflated and where it is honest.

Subtype: Approach: reasons from scratch on a problem where old methods are slow and the stakes are low [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: An engineer asks why a nightly report takes six hours, traces the data path from source to output, and finds a pointless intermediate copy.

Subtype: Approach: spends days re-deriving what experts already know [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A junior developer reinvents a scheduling method from scratch, ignoring well-tested libraries. His clean logic costs a week and misses edge cases that others solved years ago.

Subtype: Approach: checks the literature after a reasoning attempt and merges both [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After two days, he compares his method with a standard one, keeps his insight on data layout and adopts the library for the rest.

Subtype: Approach: asks what would guarantee failure and avoids those things [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student wanting good exam results lists what would ruin them, such as all-night cramming, skipping sleep and no past papers, and builds the routine to avoid each.

Subtype: Approach: designs a team project by listing how it would fall apart [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student team lists what would spoil their project: unclear roles, last-minute merging, one person unreachable. They set roles, weekly merges and a shared contact sheet.

Subtype: Approach: only avoids bad outcomes and never defines a positive goal [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student who avoids every mistake he can think of ends up with a safe, empty plan. Avoiding failure is not the same as working toward something wanted.

Subtype: Approach: asks how to make a situation worse to spot hidden levers [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A manager with a noisy meeting culture asks what would make it worse and notes late agendas and no notes. Fixing those two makes meetings shorter and calmer.

Subtype: Approach: pairs the list of things to avoid with a positive target [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Noticing the plan is only defensive, she adds one clear aim per month, so avoidance rules serve a direction rather than becoming the whole plan.

Subtype: Approach: keeps asking why until a deeper cause appears [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A girl keeps losing her pencil box. Why? Left at school. Why? Rushed at bell. Why? Packing after the bell. So she starts packing five minutes before it.

Subtype: Approach: traces a repeated problem to its underlying cause [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student failing maths tests asks why: careless errors, because rushed, because time ran out, because early questions were slow. The fix is practising early topics for speed.

Subtype: Approach: acts on the root cause found rather than the symptom [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A hostel student late every morning traces it to poor sleep, then to late phone use, then to a habit of scrolling. He charges the phone outside the room.

Subtype: Approach: stops at a convenient answer and blames a person [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: After a software outage, a team asks why once and says a colleague made a mistake. The deeper causes, missing tests and unclear review, remain and the outage recurs.

Subtype: Approach: continues asking until a process cause appears and fixes the process [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The team revisits the outage and asks why five times. They find a missing check in deployment and add an automated test rather than assigning blame.

Subtype: Approach: shouts out many ideas together before choosing one [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Asked how to decorate the classroom for a festival, children call out flowers, lamps, paper chains and rangoli. The teacher writes all of them, then the class votes for two.

Subtype: Approach: generates a big list first and judges it afterwards [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A group planning a school skit writes twenty story ideas without arguing, then crosses out those needing too many props, and keeps three to try out.

Subtype: Approach: generates ideas alone before sharing so early voices do not dominate [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A club captain asks members to jot ideas silently for five minutes before discussion, and a shy member's suggestion for a quiz format becomes the choice.

Subtype: Approach: criticises ideas during the generating phase and cuts the flow [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: In a college brainstorm, someone says that will never work after each idea, and soon nobody speaks. Only safe, familiar suggestions reach the list.

Subtype: Approach: separates a generation round from a selection round with agreed criteria [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A product manager notices a stalled meeting, sets ten minutes of no-criticism ideas, then applies three criteria, cost, time and user need, to pick candidates.

Subtype: Approach: reframes the problem to use an unexpected feature [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy cannot reach a ball under a sofa with his hand. He reframes it from reaching to pushing it out, and uses a long ruler from his bag.
A student sure he needs a big table to display his model realises the display could hang from the wall. The assumption of needing a table was never a real rule.

Subtype: Approach: changes the question from making it faster to removing the step [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Instead of speeding up a manual attendance sheet, a student volunteer replaces it with a QR check-in that removes the copying step altogether.

Subtype: Approach: turns a clever reframe into a plan that ignores practical limits [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young founder reframes a delivery problem as a barter network, an interesting idea, but does not test whether neighbours would actually trade or trust it.

Subtype: Approach: keeps the fresh idea and tests it with one small pilot [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Told the barter idea is untested, she runs a two-week trial in one lane and learns which parts people accept, then adjusts the idea from evidence.

Subtype: Approach: postpones a heated decision until emotions settle [Action]
Human Learning & Development: After a quarrel with a friend, a teenager drafts an angry message but waits a night. By morning he writes a calmer note asking to talk.

Subtype: Approach: puts a stuck problem aside overnight and returns fresh [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student stuck on a design decision leaves it after dinner, sleeps, and next morning sees that a simpler layout solves it. Rest let his mind reorganise the problem.

Subtype: Approach: uses waiting as a way to avoid a needed decision [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student says he will sleep on a college application choice for weeks. The deadline passes because incubation had no end date and nothing new was gathered.

Subtype: Approach: sleeps on a big offer after gathering the facts [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A professional receives a job offer, lists pros and cons, then waits one night before answering so that excitement does not decide alone.

Subtype: Approach: sets a decision time and a small question to reflect on [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Realising she keeps postponing, she decides she will answer by Thursday noon and writes down one question to think about overnight.

Subtype: Approach: gives a task a fixed time slot [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy sets a timer for twenty minutes for maths homework and stops when it rings, taking a short break before the next subject.

Subtype: Approach: fills a weekly timetable with slots for subjects [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A Class 10 student divides the evening into forty-minute blocks for each subject with breaks between, and marks the blocks on a wall chart.

Subtype: Approach: caps a task at a set time to fight perfectionism [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student writing a report gives the introduction one hour. When time ends he moves on, knowing he can polish later, and finishes the draft the same day.

Subtype: Approach: packs the schedule so tightly that one overrun ruins the day [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young employee boxes every hour of his day with no gaps. A single long call pushes everything back and he abandons the whole schedule by noon.

Subtype: Approach: adjusts box lengths from tracked actuals and adds gaps [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After two weeks of noting how long tasks really take, she lengthens the report block and adds a fifteen-minute gap after meetings.

Subtype: Approach: ticks off items on a list before leaving [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A girl keeps a school bag checklist on the door: books, water bottle, lunch box, homework. She ticks each item before she goes out.

Subtype: Approach: builds a checklist after forgetting something important [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After forgetting his admit card once, a student writes a list of documents and pens for every exam day and checks it the night before.

Subtype: Approach: uses a checklist for a repeated multi-step process [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A lab assistant follows a checklist for setting up an experiment, so steps in the right order are not skipped even when tired or hurried.

Subtype: Approach: ticks boxes without thinking, so the list hides new problems [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A technician runs the usual checklist and signs off, but the new machine has a different fault that no line covers. The list gave false confidence.

Subtype: Approach: reviews and updates the checklist after each incident [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After a missed step in a client release, the team adds a line for it and removes two that no longer apply, so the list stays useful and short.

Subtype: Approach: pairs a trigger with an action [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy decides that if he sees his shoes by the door after school, then he puts them on the rack. The trigger reminds him without effort.

Subtype: Approach: prepares an if-then reply to handle peer pressure [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager plans that if friends offer to skip class, then he says he has a test and leaves. Deciding beforehand makes the words easier to say.

Subtype: Approach: attaches a new habit to an existing cue [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student decides that after brushing teeth in the morning, he revises five flashcards. The habit hooks onto an already stable routine.

Subtype: Approach: writes so many rules that none can be recalled [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young manager makes dozens of if-then rules for her week. When a busy day comes she remembers none and reverts to reacting to the loudest request.

Subtype: Approach: keeps three key if-then rules and revises them when they fail [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She reduces to three rules, notices the after-lunch one is ignored, and moves the trigger to when she closes her laptop at four.

Subtype: Approach: imagines the steps before acting, sometimes out loud [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A child about to carry a glass of water says out loud, walk slow, hold with two hands, put it down. Picturing the steps helps her avoid a spill.

Subtype: Approach: rehearses a speech in the mind and in front of a mirror [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A girl preparing a class talk imagines the room, practises the opening line in front of the mirror, and notices where she forgets the second point.

Subtype: Approach: imagines the route and timings of an event day [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student walking through the interview day in his head, from bus to waiting room, realises he had not planned where to keep his file dry in the monsoon.

Subtype: Approach: imagines only the successful path and ignores obstacles [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student pictures a perfect presentation, applause and all, and never rehearses what to do if the projector fails. The simulation made him feel ready without preparing him.

Subtype: Approach: simulates both success and things going wrong and prepares a response [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A presenter adds a run-through of a dead laptop and a tough question, and carries a printed copy of the slides and a short prepared answer.

Subtype: Approach: asks what if for the main risks and writes a plan B [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager organising a cricket match asks what if it rains and arranges an indoor game or a reserved date with the school, so the day is not lost.

Subtype: Approach: prepares a backup for the likely thing that could go wrong [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student travelling for an exam by train books a bus option as well, and notes the timings, in case the train is delayed by fog.

Subtype: Approach: sets triggers for switching to plan B [Action]
Human Learning & Development: An event organiser decides that if fewer than sixty confirmations arrive by Friday, then she will move to the smaller hall, rather than deciding under pressure on the day.

Subtype: Approach: plans for so many scenarios that the main plan is neglected [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A project lead writes backup plans for twelve risks, many of them unlikely, and runs out of time to prepare the main path, which then falters.

Subtype: Approach: prunes the list to the few likely, costly risks and revisits after each phase [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The lead keeps three contingencies with clear triggers and reviews them at each milestone, dropping any that no longer apply.

Subtype: Approach: leaves extra time before something starts [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy who takes twenty minutes to reach the bus stop leaves at thirty because last week a friend stopped him to talk and he nearly missed the bus.

Subtype: Approach: adds buffer days before a deadline [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a project due on the fifteenth aims to finish by the tenth, knowing printing and unexpected illness often delay things.

Subtype: Approach: keeps some money aside in a monthly budget for surprises [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student living on an allowance sets aside a small portion for unplanned costs, such as a repair, so that one surprise does not empty the month.

Subtype: Approach: pads every task so heavily that work expands to fill it [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A colleague adds a large buffer to every estimate, and the team relaxes and finishes at the last minute anyway. The padding never turned into saved time.

Subtype: Approach: keeps one shared buffer at the end of the project [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The team removes padding from tasks and holds a single buffer before the deadline, using it only when a real delay occurs.

Subtype: Approach: builds a simple version first and improves it [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy making a model house first builds a plain cardboard box with a roof, shows his teacher, and then adds windows and paint on later days.

Subtype: Approach: releases a small first version and asks users for feedback [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager building a quiz app for classmates ships ten questions first, watches which ones friends skip, then adds more of the popular topic.

Subtype: Approach: decides the smallest useful version and defers extras [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student team building a campus notes site decides that upload and search are enough for launch, and pushes ratings and profiles to a later list.

Subtype: Approach: ships something too thin to be useful and learns little [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A founder releases a version so bare that testers cannot try the core idea. Feedback is about missing basics, not about whether the idea has value.

Subtype: Approach: revises the minimum to include the core value and repeats short cycles [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After weak feedback, she adds the one feature that made the idea worthwhile and runs two-week cycles, changing things based on what users actually do.

Subtype: Approach: changes one variable and measures the result [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student testing whether music helps study times himself doing the same sums with and without music across a week, and records the scores in a table.

Subtype: Approach: forms a hypothesis, sets a measure and runs a small test [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student running a campus club guesses that posters outperform WhatsApp for turnout, sends each in different weeks, and counts how many attend.

Subtype: Approach: draws firm conclusions from too few results [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student tries a new study method for two days, sees a small improvement, and declares it works. Two data points cannot separate the method from luck.

Subtype: Approach: runs a pilot with a small group before a full rollout [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A young manager tests a new shift schedule with one team for a month, tracking absences and handover errors, before applying it to the whole floor.

Subtype: Approach: extends the trial and adds a comparison group after doubting the result [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Doubting her early result, she continues for four weeks, keeps a control period, and finds the gain was smaller than first thought but still real.

Subtype: Approach: draws a picture of the problem to think through it [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A girl solving a word problem about sharing sweets draws circles for children and dots for sweets, and sees the answer as the leftover dots.

Subtype: Approach: writes a list to free up working memory [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student with many tasks before exams writes them all down. Seeing the list on paper lowers worry and lets him sort them into today and later.

Subtype: Approach: sketches a mind map to see how parts connect [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a thesis draws boxes and arrows for chapters, sources and questions, and notices that two chapters depend on the same data.

Subtype: Approach: keeps writing notes without acting on them [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional fills notebooks with plans and diagrams but never starts. The writing feels like progress while the first concrete step remains undone.

Subtype: Approach: reviews the page and circles one next action [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She looks over her plans, circles the single step that can be done tomorrow, and puts a time beside it so the notes turn into work.

Subtype: Approach: gives a part of the task to someone who can do it [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy organising a class quiz asks a friend who writes neatly to make the score chart, while he prepares the questions.

Subtype: Approach: assigns jobs by each person's strengths [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student captain planning a school event asks one member with good handwriting for posters and another with good contacts for permissions.

Subtype: Approach: hands over a task with clear expectations and a check-in time [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student lead gives a teammate the data cleaning, explains the format needed, and agrees to look at a sample by Wednesday.

Subtype: Approach: hands off work but keeps redoing it because it is not done her way [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A new team lead delegates a report but rewrites it entirely. The colleague feels distrusted and she ends up doing double work.

Subtype: Approach: agrees what good looks like, then steps back and gives feedback [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The lead states the outcome needed, lets the colleague choose the method, and gives feedback on the result, which improves quality and trust.

Subtype: Approach: brings a problem to a caregiver [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A toddler holds a toy with a stuck lid up to her mother and whimpers. The caregiver is used as a tool to solve a problem the child cannot manage.

Subtype: Approach: asks a trusted adult a direct question [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A child who cannot tie shoelaces asks his grandfather to show him, watches slowly, then tries with the grandfather's hands guiding his.

Subtype: Approach: seeks a teacher when stuck after trying alone [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A girl tries a maths problem for a while, then takes it to the teacher with her attempt, so the teacher can see where her thinking went wrong.

Subtype: Approach: prepares questions before meeting a professional [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a career visits an alumnus with three written questions on skills, entry paths and daily work, and takes notes to compare later.

Subtype: Approach: treats an expert's view as final without asking the reasons [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young entrepreneur follows an adviser's suggestion on pricing without understanding why, and misses that the adviser's market differs from her own.

Subtype: Approach: asks for the reasoning and checks it against a second source [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She asks the adviser why, checks with another practitioner, and adapts the advice to her own customers.

Subtype: Approach: asks several friends for suggestions [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy wanting a name for his cricket team asks five friends and his cousin, writes down all the names and picks the one that made everyone laugh.

Subtype: Approach: polls a class group for options [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student posts in the class group asking for ideas for the farewell gift, collects thirty replies, and sorts them into a few themes.

Subtype: Approach: collects suggestions from a wide community and looks for repeated patterns [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student club posts a question online about fresher orientation problems and notes that many replies mention confusion about hostel rules.

Subtype: Approach: takes the most upvoted idea without checking it fits [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A small business owner runs a poll on social media and adopts the top choice. Voters are not her customers and the product does not sell.

Subtype: Approach: weighs the answers by who gave them and tests the top few [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She narrows the answers to those from actual customers, tries two of them in small batches, and keeps the one buyers actually pick.

Subtype: Approach: works out what each side wants and finds a swap [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Two siblings both want the study table at the same time. The girl wants it after dinner and the boy in the afternoon, so they agree on split hours.

Subtype: Approach: separates a demand from the interest behind it [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager wanting to stay late at a friend's house realises his parents' worry is safe travel, and offers to be picked up by his cousin.

Subtype: Approach: prepares options and a fallback before talking [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student negotiating with roommates about chores lists several rota options in advance and knows what she can accept, so the talk is calm.

Subtype: Approach: treats it as winner takes all and damages the relationship [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A team member insists on his schedule and wins the argument, but colleagues stop cooperating and later favours are refused.

Subtype: Approach: asks what the other side needs and reshapes the deal [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After a stalemate, she asks the vendor what matters most, learns it is quick payment, and trades earlier payment for a lower price.

Subtype: Approach: picks the plan that fits what matters most to them [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy invited to two parties chooses his grandmother's birthday because being with family matters more to him than the cricket match.

Subtype: Approach: names what matters before choosing a path [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student choosing between coaching for a rank and a music course lists what he values, creativity and independence, and chooses accordingly with parents' input.

Subtype: Approach: checks each option against a short list of personal values [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student weighing internships writes honesty, learning and family time as values, then rejects an offer with long unpaid hours that would erode them.

Subtype: Approach: follows a stated value without checking real constraints [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional wanting to serve rural communities quits her job with no savings or plan. The value was sound but the plan ignored her family obligations.

Subtype: Approach: keeps the value and rebuilds the route in stages [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She returns to work part time, saves for a year, and volunteers on weekends with a rural health group before deciding on a bigger shift.

Subtype: Approach: goes to a calm spot when upset before trying again [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A child frustrated with a puzzle pushes it away, goes to sit with his mother for a while, and returns to try again once he is calmer.

Subtype: Approach: picks an easier task when tired or upset [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A girl who is worried before a test does a favourite drawing for ten minutes first to calm down, then begins revision.

Subtype: Approach: schedules hard work at the times of day when energy is highest [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager notices he thinks best in the early morning, so he does maths then and keeps evenings for lighter revision and reading.

Subtype: Approach: makes big decisions while angry or anxious [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: After a poor result, a student decides in a rage to drop his branch. A week later, calmer, he sees the choice was driven by shame more than by facts.

Subtype: Approach: names the feeling, waits, and then plans [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Feeling overwhelmed by a deadline, she says I feel anxious, takes a walk, and returns to sort tasks into a short list, which lowers the pressure.

Subtype: Approach: sees which tasks must finish before others can start [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student planning a science exhibition sees that the model cannot be painted before it dries, and that the report needs the results, so those come first.

Subtype: Approach: maps the longest chain of dependent tasks to see the minimum time [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student team charting a project finds that data collection, analysis and report form the longest chain, so any delay there delays everything.

Subtype: Approach: starts long-lead items early and does small tasks in the gaps [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A wedding planner orders the printed cards, which take two weeks, before anything else, and fills waiting time with vendor calls.

Subtype: Approach: focuses on the visible tasks and ignores a hidden dependency [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A project team polishes the app screens but forgets that the payment gateway approval takes a month. The launch date slips because of a task nobody had listed.

Subtype: Approach: redraws the path when a delay appears and shifts resources [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: When the approval slips, the lead moves two developers onto the tasks that now determine the end date and lets non-critical items wait.
A girl washes all her brushes after painting, and puts away all the colours at once, rather than tidying after each colour.

Subtype: Approach: groups similar homework into one session [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student does all reading tasks together and then all writing tasks, finding that switching subjects often wastes his time and focus.

Subtype: Approach: batches errands into one trip [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A hostel student lists stationery, laundry and a bank visit and does all in a single trip to town rather than three separate ones.

Subtype: Approach: batches emails in fixed slots to protect deep work [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A developer checks messages at eleven and four and keeps the morning free for coding, so he is not interrupted throughout the day.

Subtype: Approach: batches so long that urgent matters wait too long [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A manager answers messages only once a day, and a colleague's urgent question about a client sits unanswered until evening.

Subtype: Approach: keeps batches but adds a quick way to reach her for urgent items [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She keeps her two mail slots and shares a phone number for urgent matters, so focus is kept without blocking real emergencies.

Subtype: Approach: makes a public promise to keep on track [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager tells his class group he will finish a coding tutorial in a month. Not wanting to look foolish, he sets a daily hour.
A student before exams deletes a game from his phone and gives his charger to a roommate at night, so distraction is harder than study.

Subtype: Approach: pays or books something in advance to create a cost for quitting [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A young worker pays for a three-month gym plan upfront, knowing money already spent makes him more likely to attend.

Subtype: Approach: sets a device so strict that it backfires [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A worker locks himself out of all apps for the whole day, then needs one for work, breaks the lock in a hurry and abandons the whole system.

Subtype: Approach: loosens the rule and keeps the parts that helped [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: He keeps the evening block on games and allows work apps during the day, so the device supports the goal without getting in the way.

Subtype: Approach: studies with a friend who has a similar goal [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager pairs with a classmate for evening study calls. Knowing someone is waiting makes him start on time even on lazy days.

Subtype: Approach: agrees to report progress to a friend [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Two students preparing for the same exam text each other their hours studied each night, and feel motivated to keep the streak going.

Subtype: Approach: picks a partner who excuses everything [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student partners with a close friend who always says it is fine, take a break. The check-ins turn into shared excuses and nothing changes.

Subtype: Approach: asks a colleague to check milestones weekly [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional writing a certification plan meets a colleague every Friday to show what was done, which helps her keep to the schedule.

Subtype: Approach: chooses a partner who is kind but firm and sets clear questions [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She swaps to a senior colleague who asks what was done and what is next, and both agree on a short weekly format so it stays honest.

Subtype: Approach: drops a project that is not working after some effort [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy stops building a big model after realising the glue will not hold, and starts a smaller design instead of pouring in more days.

Subtype: Approach: considers what has already been spent and decides based on what lies ahead [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student who has done six months of a course he dislikes asks whether the next six months are worth it, rather than whether the first six were wasted.

Subtype: Approach: sets a review point in advance to decide whether to continue [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A student starting a side project decides that if no users appear by month three, he will stop and use the time for placement preparation.

Subtype: Approach: keeps going only because so much has been invested [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A founder continues a failing product for two years because of money and effort already spent, even after users leave and no path to recovery is visible.

Subtype: Approach: stops, records the lessons and redirects the effort [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: The founder closes the product, writes what he learned about the market and the team, and uses those lessons in a new smaller venture.

Subtype: Approach: grabs the object first without thinking [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A toddler sees a bright toy on the table and reaches out at once, knocking over a glass. The wish leads directly to the action without any planning in between.

Subtype: Approach: acts on the first idea and then regrets [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A child cuts his own fringe with scissors because he wants to look like his cousin. He did not think about what would happen if it went wrong.

Subtype: Approach: learns to pause and count before acting [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After blurting an answer and getting it wrong, a boy learns to count to three and check the question again before he answers in class.

Subtype: Approach: buys something on a sudden urge [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager spends his festival money on a gadget he sees in an advertisement, and later cannot afford the notebook and book fee he needed.

Subtype: Approach: puts a waiting rule on spending decisions [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A student adopts a rule that anything costing over a set amount must wait two days. Most urges pass, and the few real needs remain.

Subtype: Approach: uses quick action deliberately when the situation is urgent and stakes are small [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A colleague sees a spill in the corridor and mops it at once instead of planning. Speed was the right choice because it was simple and immediate.

Subtype: Approach: repeats the same method although it is not working [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A boy keeps pushing a jammed drawer harder and harder. He does not try lifting it or checking what is stuck, so nothing changes.

Subtype: Approach: keeps studying the same way despite poor results [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student re-reads notes for hours before every exam and scores poorly, but does not try self-testing because rereading has always been his way.

Subtype: Approach: notices no progress and asks what could be different [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After a low mark, he asks what he could change, tries practice questions, and finds recalling works better than re-reading.

Subtype: Approach: sticks with a plan out of pride even after the facts change [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student leader insists on the original event date after the venue cancels, and refuses to consider a change because she announced it publicly.

Subtype: Approach: keeps a firm goal but changes the method [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Told the road route is blocked, a manager keeps the delivery date but shifts to rail, showing persistence on the goal and flexibility on the means.

Subtype: Approach: persistence as a strength on a hard long task [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A researcher keeps refining an experiment through many failures, because prior results suggest the effect is real. She adjusts details each time rather than repeating them.

Subtype: Approach: fears making the wrong choice and keeps gathering data [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager choosing an elective keeps asking more people and reading more articles, hoping for a choice that has no risk, though none exists.

Subtype: Approach: compares options endlessly without deciding [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student reads reviews of twenty laptops for three weeks and still cannot choose. New information keeps adding doubt rather than clarity.

Subtype: Approach: asks what a good enough choice would be and what reversing it would cost [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Realising the choice can be changed later, a student picks a reasonable option and moves on, saving time for things that matter more.

Subtype: Approach: sets a deadline and a limit on how many options to consider [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional decides to look at three options and choose by Sunday. The limit turns an open search into a task with an end.

Subtype: Approach: uses a trusted friend to break the tie [Action]
Human Learning & Development: Stuck between two flats, she asks a friend who knows her habits to choose. Handing the tie-break over ends the loop.

Subtype: Approach: enjoys making plans more than doing the work [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager designs elaborate study charts because planning feels good and gives a sense of progress, while the actual chapters remain unread.

Subtype: Approach: builds a detailed plan for months ahead and delays starting [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student spends two weeks colour-coding a study timetable for the whole semester and starts studying only afterwards, with less time left than before.

Subtype: Approach: starts a rough version early to learn what matters [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A student stops planning and builds a rough draft in one afternoon. The draft shows which parts needed planning and which did not.

Subtype: Approach: plans every hour and cannot adapt when things change [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A young manager makes a minute-by-minute plan for a conference trip. A flight delay breaks the whole plan and she feels lost without it.

Subtype: Approach: plans the next step in detail and leaves later steps loose [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Noticing the plan cracks each week, she plans in detail only for the coming week and sets rough goals for the rest of the month.

Subtype: Approach: believes a wish or a ritual will cause the result [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A child believes that wearing his lucky red shirt will make his team win, and refuses to change even when it is dirty.

Subtype: Approach: hopes that it will somehow work out without acting [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A girl leaves her project until the last night, telling herself it will be fine, and hopes the teacher will extend the date.

Subtype: Approach: relies on a lucky routine on exam day [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager carries the same pen and touches a temple wall before every exam. It calms him, though he also studies, so the ritual supports rather than replaces effort.

Subtype: Approach: expects things to work because they should [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student assumes that because he works hard, the interview will go well, and does no preparation. Effort in general did not cover the specific questions asked.

Subtype: Approach: separates comforting rituals from the concrete steps that actually matter [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: After a failed attempt, she keeps her calming ritual but adds mock tests and feedback, so comfort no longer stands in for preparation.

Subtype: Approach: puts off an unpleasant task by doing something easy [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A boy with a hard maths worksheet suddenly tidies his bookshelf and sharpens every pencil. The task he fears stays untouched.

Subtype: Approach: delays because the task feels too big [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager with a long essay keeps scrolling on his phone. The size of the task makes him feel small, so he avoids even opening the file.

Subtype: Approach: starts with two minutes to get going [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A student stuck avoiding a report tells himself he will open the file and write one sentence. Starting is the hard part, and he keeps writing for an hour.

Subtype: Approach: avoids a difficult conversation and lets the problem grow [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A colleague delays telling a teammate about a mistake. The problem grows until the client notices, and the talk becomes harder than it would have been.

Subtype: Approach: names the fear behind the delay and takes a small step [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: She notices she is afraid of criticism, writes a short honest message, and sends it. The relief is greater than the worry she had before.

Subtype: Approach: copies a friend's way of doing something [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A boy copies his friend's way of arranging his cricket kit. It works for his friend, who has a big bag, but not for his small one.

Subtype: Approach: adopts a topper's study schedule [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager copies a topper's five-am routine though he is a night person, and ends up sleepy in class and with poorer marks.

Subtype: Approach: follows friends into the same course without checking his own interest [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student picks the same engineering branch as his friends because it feels safe. He later finds he has little interest in the subjects.

Subtype: Approach: tests borrowed methods on a small scale and keeps what fits [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Trying a friend's note-taking method for a week, a student keeps the summary box idea and drops the colour codes that slow him down.

Subtype: Approach: copies a successful company's plan without its context [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A small start-up copies a large firm's hiring process, though it has three employees and no budget, and wastes weeks on steps it does not need.

Subtype: Approach: asks why something worked for them and what is different here [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Before copying a rival's pricing, she asks what conditions made it work and finds her customers, costs and location differ, so she adapts it.

Subtype: Approach: thinks a task will take only a few minutes [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A boy says he will finish his drawing in ten minutes before dinner. It takes an hour, and he ends up upset when his mother calls.

Subtype: Approach: repeats the same underestimate again and again [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager plans to finish revision for a whole subject in one weekend, and misses each time, yet makes the same weekend plan for the next subject.

Subtype: Approach: estimates from the best case and expects to finish early [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student thinks a project will take three days if all goes well, and it takes ten with interruptions, a broken laptop and unclear steps.

Subtype: Approach: uses past similar tasks to estimate time [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A developer looks at how long three earlier features actually took, adds a margin, and gives a realistic estimate rather than a hopeful guess.

Subtype: Approach: splits a task into smaller parts and times each [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Rather than guess a week for a report, she estimates each section separately and finds it will take nearly two, and tells her manager early.

Subtype: Approach: friends make a plan and nobody questions the risks [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A group of friends plans a late trip to a waterfall. Each privately worries about safety, but all assume the others are fine with it.

Subtype: Approach: assigns one member to question the plan [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A student team picks a devil's advocate for each meeting, and the questions reveal a gap in the budget before it becomes a problem.

Subtype: Approach: goes along with the group because no one wants to disagree [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A team agrees to an unrealistic launch date because the leader is keen. Several members have doubts but stay quiet, and the date is missed.

Subtype: Approach: collects opinions privately before discussion [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: A manager asks for written views before the meeting, so junior members' concerns appear without being shaped by what the seniors say.

Subtype: Approach: invites an outsider to review the plan [Action]
Human Learning & Development: The team asks a colleague from another department to read the launch plan, and she spots an assumption everyone had shared without noticing.

Subtype: Approach: uses trial and error for a small new puzzle [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A boy facing a new board game with no rules explained just tries moves and sees what happens, since mistakes cost nothing and playing is the point.

Subtype: Approach: asks an adult when the problem is unsafe or too big [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A girl who finds a snake in the garden does not try to deal with it herself but calls her father, since the situation calls for an adult.

Subtype: Approach: uses a checklist for a familiar routine task [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student who packs for the same school trips each term uses a fixed list. For a repeated task with known steps, a routine is faster than fresh thinking.

Subtype: Approach: makes a careful plan when the stakes are high [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager applying for a scholarship plans each step, checks documents twice and asks a teacher to review, because errors here are costly and not easily undone.

Subtype: Approach: asks an expert when the problem is outside his knowledge [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager with a health-related question about sports training asks a coach and a doctor rather than guess from social media.

Subtype: Approach: uses time-boxing when a task is dull and easy to postpone [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student who avoids chemistry practice sets a twenty-five minute timer, since a small bounded start suits a task he tends to put off.

Subtype: Approach: picks a quick rough sketch when the problem is new and the time is short [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A teenager asked at short notice to design a fest banner sketches three quick layouts in ten minutes and picks one, since a polished plan would waste the time available.

Subtype: Approach: acts quickly when time is short and the situation is urgent [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student sees a friend faint at a hostel event and acts at once, calling for help, since there is no time for a detailed plan.

Subtype: Approach: takes time and sleeps on it when the decision is slow and important [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student weighing whether to pursue further study lets the decision take a month, gathering facts and talking to family, since no deadline forces speed.

Subtype: Approach: plans alone for a personal decision [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student choosing his own study schedule thinks it through alone, since he knows his own habits and others' input would add little.

Subtype: Approach: plans as a group when several people share the result [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A hostel floor deciding on shared rules holds a meeting, since a plan made by one person alone would not be accepted or followed by the rest.

Subtype: Approach: uses one method for every problem out of habit [Pitfall]
Human Learning & Development: A student who likes detailed timetables uses them even for creative work, where a loose start would suit better, and feels blocked.

Subtype: Approach: uses working backward when there is a fixed date [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student with a fixed submission date counts back from it to set weekly targets, since the deadline defines the goal.

Subtype: Approach: matches effort to reversibility, deciding fast on reversible choices and slow on one-way ones [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A student picks a phone plan quickly because he can change it next month, but takes weeks over a long-term rental contract that is hard to leave.

Subtype: Approach: uses brainstorming for a novel problem with no known answer [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A team facing a new customer problem gathers many ideas before choosing, as there is no precedent to copy and diverse thinking helps.

Subtype: Approach: uses precedent for a familiar problem [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: An experienced coordinator plans a routine workshop by reusing last year's schedule, changing only dates and venue, since the problem is well understood.

Subtype: Approach: uses a light minimum version for a low-stakes, uncertain idea [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A colleague testing a new newsletter sends one simple issue rather than designing a full system, since the cost of being wrong is low.

Subtype: Approach: uses a pre-mortem and contingency plan for a high-stakes irreversible move [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: Before a house purchase, a couple imagines how it could go wrong, checks legal papers, and keeps a reserve fund, because the choice is hard to undo.

Subtype: Approach: uses a decision matrix when several options are close and reasons must be shown [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A manager choosing between three vendors scores them on agreed criteria, so the decision can be explained to others and is not seen as personal preference.

Subtype: Approach: uses satisficing for a minor choice, saving effort for the important ones [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A professional picks the first suitable lunch place near the office, and keeps her careful analysis for the job change she is considering.

Subtype: Approach: notices the method is not matching the problem and switches [Revision]
Human Learning & Development: Finding her careful plan is stalling an unclear project, a manager switches to a quick prototype to learn more before planning further.

Subtype: Approach: uses experiments when the answer depends on real users [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A product team unsure whether customers want a feature runs a small test with a few users instead of debating, since only data will settle it.

Subtype: Approach: combines methods in one project: brainstorm, matrix, then a checklist [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A team generates ideas, scores them on a matrix, then turns the chosen plan into a checklist, using each method where it fits best.

Subtype: Approach: takes advice from a group when a decision affects many and needs buy-in [Thinking]
Human Learning & Development: A department head consults her team about a new shift system, since their acceptance decides whether it works, even if it takes longer.

Subtype: Approach: slows down and involves a lawyer or professional when the matter is legal or financial and unfamiliar [Action]
Human Learning & Development: A young professional facing an unfamiliar property dispute does not improvise. She gathers the papers and consults a qualified professional, since general reasoning is not enough here.
